title: Beyond Content: Integrating Generated User Intent and Planned Behavior Theory for Reliable Fake News Detection

problem.claim: Generative AI has made the boundary between authentic and deceptive content increasingly ambiguous, challenging fake news detection methods based only on observable content or propagation structures.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often neglect the psychological motivations behind user behavior, while user decision-making is unobservable and difficult for conventional deep learning models to represent.

contributions.claim: The authors propose TPB-VAE, a psychologically grounded framework that integrates the Theory of Planned Behavior with large language models to infer and encode users' latent intent.
TPB-VAE maps Theory of Planned Behavior constructs into a latent space to make the decision-making process computationally accessible.
The framework uses semi-supervised learning to infer latent user intent from a small subset of labeled samples and derives behavioral features from those intents for fake news detection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on four real-world datasets.
The authors report that their approach is effective and adversarially resilient.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative AI complicates the distinction between authentic and deceptive content for traditional fake news detection.
Content- and propagation-focused approaches overlook psychological motivations, and latent decision-making is difficult to capture because it is unobservable.
TPB-VAE combines the Theory of Planned Behavior with large language models to infer and encode latent user intent.
The framework maps behavioral constructs into latent space and uses semi-supervised learning with limited labeled data to derive behavioral features.
The authors report extensive experiments on four real-world datasets showing effectiveness and adversarial resilience.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses semi-supervised learning to infer latent user intent from a small labeled subset.

interpretation.claim: When psychologically meaningful variables are difficult to observe directly, limited labels may be used to construct latent behavioral representations.

application.claim: Apply semi-supervised latent-intent modeling when user motivations are unobservable and labeled behavioral data are scarce.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond fake news detection or remains reliable with different labeling regimes.

unknowns: The four datasets and their domains are unspecified.
Evaluation metrics, baselines, effect sizes, and statistical details are unspecified.
The adversarial threat model and resilience evaluation procedure are unspecified.
The labeled-sample size and semi-supervised training procedure are unspecified.
The mapping from Theory of Planned Behavior constructs to latent variables is unspecified.
